title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (previous page, item 'Récapitulons'). The data are: X of finite type over Q̄; a normal-crossings divisor D = Σ_{i∈I} D_i; a set J ⊂ X'(Q̄) of marked points, with X' = X − D. Then 𝒢' = Aut_scheme(X; D, J), meaning semilinear automorphisms not required to be over Q̄. G' ⊂ 𝒢' is the subgroup of Q̄-linear automorphisms, T(Q̄) = lim μ_n, and Γ = Gal(Q̄/Q).

This page.
(1) Restricting a scheme automorphism to Q̄ gives the exact sequence 1 → G' → 𝒢' → Γ. Its image is the stabilizer in Γ of the isomorphism class of (X, D, J), i.e. Gal(Q̄/field of moduli).
(2) A 'germ of lifting' is an open subgroup Γ' ⊂ Γ with a homomorphic section Γ' → 𝒢'. It is considered up to shrinking Γ'. Such a section comes from a model of (X, D, J) over a number field K, with Γ' = Gal(Q̄/K). Different models give different germs.
(III) Choose a profinite universal cover X̃' → X'; then π_1(X') = Aut(X̃'/X').
(3) Let ℰ' be the group of scheme automorphisms of X̃' lifting elements of 𝒢'. Since X̃' is universal, every element of 𝒢' lifts, which gives 1 → π_1(X') → ℰ' → 𝒢' → 1. Pulled back along Γ' (via the germ) this is the usual arithmetic fundamental group π_1(X'_K). Pulled back along G' it is the geometric orbifold fundamental group of [X'/G'].
(4) ℰ' acts on two sets:
- X̃'(I): the 'points at infinity' of X̃' over the components D_i, i.e. points of the normalization of X in X̃' over the generic points of the D_i, which index the cusps or branches.
- X̃'(J): the points of the pro-cover lying over the marked points.
(5) The natural ℰ'-equivariant maps are X̃'(I) → I and X̃'(J) → J ≅ X̃'(J)/π_1. Here ℰ' acts on I and J through 𝒢'.

Next page. Each point of X̃'(I) gives its inertia group, a procyclic group ≅ T(Q̄) = Ẑ(1). This is encoded as an equivariant map Φ: X̃'(I) → Hom(T, π_1), compatible with the cyclotomic action through Γ. Each point over j ∈ J gives a splitting of ℰ'_j → 𝒢'_j (a decomposition section), encoded as Ψ.

Purpose. Together these data form a purely group-theoretic 'paradigm' of the marked, punctured variety (X, D, J). It is an anabelian encoding: extension, cusp inertia, rational-point sections, cyclotomic character, plus symmetry group and Galois germ. Presumably it is meant to be compared with combinatorial or Teichmüller-type objects, as in 'Paradigmes des courbes algébriques'.
errors: 𝒢' → Γ is not surjective in general (no '→1' is written, correctly). Its image is Gal(Q̄/M), where M is the field of moduli of (X, D, J).

A germ of lifting Γ' → 𝒢' exists only if (X, D, J) descends to a number field. This is automatic for X and D, but requires J to be finite (or Galois-stable over some number field). J ⊂ X'(Q̄) is allowed to be arbitrary in the data; the condition is not stated.
In (5) the quotient should read X̃'(J)/π_1, not X'(J)/π_1. This is probably a transcription slip.
For dim X > 1 the description by I alone ignores intersections of the D_i, where inertia is Ẑ(1)^k. Grothendieck himself flags on the next page that the higher-dimensional case needs revision.

ideas.what: Exact sequence 1→G'→𝒢'→Γ of semilinear automorphisms, with image the Galois group of the field of moduli
ideas.modern_name: field of moduli / automorphism–Galois exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weil descent; Shimura; Coombes–Harbater and Dèbes–Douai for covers

ideas.what: Germ of section Γ'→𝒢' over an open subgroup, encoding a model over a number field up to finite extension
ideas.modern_name: model / descent datum up to finite extension (germ of Galois action)

ideas.what: Extension 1→π_1(X')→ℰ'→𝒢'→1 using automorphisms of the universal pro-cover, combining Galois action and geometric symmetries
ideas.modern_name: arithmetic fundamental group of the quotient stack [X'/G'] over the field of moduli; fundamental exact sequence
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck SGA1 (fundamental exact sequence); orbifold version folklore and Dèbes–Douai
ideas.where_published: SGA1 IX (homotopy exact sequence); Esquisse d'un programme (anabelian, Galois–Teichmüller)

ideas.what: ℰ'-sets of points of the universal cover above the divisor components and above the marked points, with equivariant maps to I and J; leads to inertia maps and decomposition-section maps
ideas.modern_name: cuspidal inertia subgroups and decomposition sections (section conjecture data); 'tame anabelian datum' with cusps and marked points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, letter to Faltings 1983 / Esquisse 1984; later Nakamura, Mochizuki, Hoshi
ideas.where_published: Letter to Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984), in less formalized form

missed.claim: This is an early (c. 1980–81), explicit formalization of the full 'anabelian paradigm' of a marked punctured variety, predating the Faltings letter and the Esquisse. It packages arithmetic π_1 together with the geometric automorphism group 𝒢', cusp-inertia data and marked-point sections into one equivariant group-theoretic object. Its components are all known individually. The specific package (using 𝒢' rather than just Γ, plus a germ of Galois lifting) is a documented precursor and a small historical datum.
missed.quote: structure d'extension 1 → π_1(𝒳') → ℰ' → 𝒢' → 1 ... ℰ'-ensembles 𝒳̃'(I), 𝒳̃'(J)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It dates Grothendieck's anabelian formalism with marked points and symmetries earlier than usually cited. It also shows him treating field of moduli vs. field of definition inside the anabelian framework.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is standard by modern standards: the fundamental exact sequence, cusp inertia, decomposition sections and the field of moduli. Interest is mainly historical, as an early systematic version of the anabelian/Teichmüller 'paradigm' datum including geometric automorphisms and marked points.
transcription_corrections: First marginal note seems to read 'relation pour mémoire avec variétés de modules des courbes de genre ...' rather than 'cycles évanescents' (uncertain).
In (5): '𝒳̃'(J) → J ≃ 𝒳̃'(J)/π_1' (tilde missing in the transcription).
Diagram (2) shows Γ' ⊂ Γ as a subgroup (vertical inclusion) with an arrow Γ' → 𝒢'; 'ss-groupe ouvert' is written next to it.
J in (4)/(5) denotes the marked-point set 𝔍 of the previous page.
